transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. It's very nice to meet you. Am I okay to sit right here? Thank you. 

Well, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. It's probably just a bit of normal stress, honestly. I'm a supervisor at a retail store, so I'm used to keeping things running smoothly and taking care of my team. But... well, lately, when I try to explain the inventory numbers to everyone, or go over the weekend schedule, my words just sort of... they start jumping around a bit. 

Like, I'll be talking about the delivery trucks, and then suddenly I'm mentioning Thursdays, or the church grill, or my boss’s tone of voice. It all connects in my head, I promise, but... people just look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying. I always want to be clear and do a good job for my team, so it's a little embarrassing when they stare at me like that. 

I'm sure it's nothing major, but I figured I should come in. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you always had this kind of way of talking, or is it something that only started recently?

Oh, no, definitely not always. I've always prided myself on being very clear with my team... you know, you really have to be when you're running a store. 

But, um... I suppose it's been... maybe about six months now? That's when these, well, these jumbled explanations started happening. And sometimes I'll just sort of... make these odd stops, right in the middle of a sentence out on the sales floor. It's really not a huge deal, I promise. It's just been a little more noticeable over the last half year or so. 

I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it actually is. I'm sure it's just the stress catching up with me. Does that timeline make sense to you, Doctor? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to notice?

Oh, um... hearing or seeing things? No, no, nothing like that. I mean, retail can be loud, you know? The music, the customers, the registers beeping. Sometimes I might think I hear my name being called over the intercom when it wasn't, but... that's just normal, right? Just the noise of the store playing tricks on you. 

But as far as, well, things other people don't notice... no, I don't think so. I'm very grounded, very focused on the reality of the store and my team. I wouldn't want you to think I'm... well, that I'm losing touch with things or anything like that. I'm just a bit stressed, that's all. Is that what you meant by that question? I hope I answered it the right way.
Have you been needing much less sleep than usual lately?

Oh, sleep? No, I don't think so. I mean, I sleep just fine, really. I try to get my full eight hours every night so I can be sharp for the morning shift. 

Sometimes I might wake up a little early if I'm thinking about the stockroom organization or something, but... well, that's just being a dedicated employee, isn't it? I definitely wouldn't say I need *less* sleep. I'm taking good care of myself, I promise. I know how important rest is. 

Does that sound alright? I hope I'm not giving you the impression that I'm running myself into the ground or anything.
Do you find yourself wanting to be around other people less than you used to?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean, my whole career is built on being a people person, right? You really can't manage a busy retail team if you don't like being around folks. 

I will say, um... sometimes after a really long shift, I might just want to sit quietly in the living room for a little bit. Just to rest my feet and recharge. But that's just normal unwinding, isn't it? I'm certainly not hiding away or isolating myself. I still chat with the neighbors and make sure I check in with all my staff every single day. I'd hate for anyone to think I was becoming anti-social or anything like that. 

I really try to keep a positive, outgoing attitude for everyone's sake. I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm doing all the right things to stay healthy and engaged. Does that sound like a normal routine to you, Doctor?
As a child, did you have trouble making friends or understanding social cues?

Oh, childhood? Um, no, I wouldn't say I had trouble. I was always pretty good at getting along with the other kids. I mean, sure, maybe I was a little quiet sometimes, like on the first day of a new grade or something, but... well, that's just normal kid stuff, right? 

I always had a nice little group of friends. You kind of learn early on how to read people, and I think that really helped me later on in my retail career. I always tried to be polite, follow the rules, and, you know, do what the teachers expected of me. I certainly wasn't the type to sit all by myself or miss the joke. 

I hope that's a good thing? I just want to assure you I had a very, um, standard upbringing. I was a good kid. Does that answer your question alright?
Have you been able to keep up with work as well as you used to?

Well, um... I mean, I always try to give a hundred and ten percent, you know? I really pride myself on my work ethic. But... I suppose things have been just a little bit trickier lately. It's nothing I can't fix, I promise. 

They did, um... well, they actually took me off the busy weekend shifts recently. I like to think they just want to give some of the younger folks a chance to step up, but... my boss did mention during my last performance review that if things don't improve, I could be facing a suspension. I was so embarrassed, to be honest with you. But I'm going to work really hard to make sure that doesn't happen. I want to be a good employee, I really do. 

And at home, my wife has been an absolute angel. She’s, um... she's had to cover a few of the commitments I usually handle. I guess maybe I was making some people a little uncomfortable, or they were getting confused around me lately? I certainly don't mean to upset anyone, of course. So she just steps in to help out. 

I'm really trying to get back to my old self so I don't let my boss or my wife down. I hope you know I'm taking all of this very seriously, Doctor. Does it sound like I'm doing the right things to get back on track?
When your speech gets jumbled, do you also find it hard to keep your thoughts organized, or is it only the way the words come out?

Well, um... I really try my best to be clear, you know? I want everyone to understand me, especially at work. But... I suppose it's a bit of both, if I'm being completely honest. 

I actually came in because, well, when I try to explain the inventory numbers to the team, or go over the weekend schedule... my mind just sort of... races? And then my words start jumping around. Like, I'll be talking about the delivery trucks, and then suddenly I'm talking about Thursdays, and then somehow I'm mentioning the grill at church, and then I'm thinking about the tone my boss used the other day... 

It's just that I have so many important things to keep track of, you know? But then people look at me like they can't follow what I'm saying at all. It's terribly embarrassing. I don't mean to confuse anyone, I promise. I really want to be a good communicator. 

I hope that makes sense? I'm trying very hard to get my thoughts lined up properly so I can explain things better. Is that a normal thing to happen when you're just under a little bit of stress at work, Doctor?
Do you ever feel like other people are watching you, talking about you, or trying to harm or control you?

Oh, no, no, definitely not. I, um... I've always had a really good relationship with the people around me, both at work and at home. I mean, sure, sometimes in retail you might get a customer who's a little grumpy or, you know, a boss who's keeping a close eye on the floor to make sure we're hitting our sales targets, but that's just normal business, right? 

I certainly don't think anyone is out to get me or control me. I've always believed that if you treat people with respect and do your job well, they'll treat you the same way in return. I try very hard to be a team player and a supportive husband. 

I wouldn't want you to think I'm paranoid or anything like that. I really just try to see the best in people. That's the right attitude to have, isn't it, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm looking at things the right way.
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are not fully your own, as if someone else can put thoughts into your mind or take them out?

Oh, goodness, no. No, my thoughts are definitely my own. I, um... I take a lot of pride in my own ideas, you know? Like when I'm coming up with a new way to organize the stockroom or planning a weekend project with my wife. 

I mean, sometimes my mind gets a little cluttered, like I mentioned before... just trying to juggle all the responsibilities at the store and at home. But it's always just me in there, doing the thinking. I've never felt like anyone else was interfering with my mind or anything strange like that. 

I try to keep a very clear head, Doctor. I want to make sure I'm staying focused and dependable for the people who count on me. It's completely normal to just feel a little overwhelmed by your own thoughts sometimes when you have a lot on your plate, right? I'm sure a lot of hardworking people feel that way.
As a child, did you have any intense, narrow interests that you spent a lot of time on?

Oh, um... no, not really. I was a very, well, a very typical boy, I think. I just liked what all the other kids liked in the neighborhood. You know, riding bikes, playing a little baseball, just being outside with my friends. I never got overly obsessed with any one particular thing or locked myself away in my room to study just one topic. 

I always tried to just fit in and get along with everyone. My parents always said I was a very easy child to raise, very agreeable. I think it's important to be well-rounded, don't you? Just having a healthy, balanced interest in normal, everyday things... that's the best way for a child to grow up, isn't it, Doctor?
Before these last six months, did you ever talk or think in a similarly hard-to-follow way?

Oh, no, definitely not. I've always prided myself on being a very clear communicator. You have to be, you know, when you're supervising a retail floor. You have to give clear directions to the team and make sure the customers understand the promotions and everything. 

I mean, maybe sometimes I'd get a little tired after a long shift and lose my train of thought for a second, but nothing out of the ordinary. Just the normal kind of tired anyone would get. I've always been very organized in my thinking and how I speak to people. 

I really try to make sure I'm making sense and being helpful to everyone around me. It's so important to be understood, don't you agree, Doctor? I wouldn't want you to think I've ever had trouble communicating properly. I've always been very capable in that department.
Have you always found it hard to understand or fit in with other people, even when you were growing up?

Oh, no, not at all. I've always been very... well, very sociable, I think. Growing up, I had plenty of friends. We'd just do regular kid things, like I mentioned before. I never felt like I didn't belong. 

And even as an adult, working in retail, you really have to be a people person to manage a team and help customers all day, you know? I've always prided myself on being easy to get along with. People seem to like me, and I always try to be polite and understanding with everyone I meet. 

It's so important to be a team player, don't you think, Doctor? I've never really felt like an outsider or had trouble understanding folks. I just want to be someone people can rely on and feel comfortable around. That's a good trait to have, isn't it?
Before these last six months, did you have a lifelong pattern of finding social interactions confusing or awkward, even if you managed to get by?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I've always been pretty good at reading people. You kind of have to be, right? When you're managing a store, you're constantly dealing with different personalities, smoothing over little disagreements, making sure the customers leave happy. 

I've never really felt... awkward, or like I didn't know what was going on in a conversation. I always try to be very attentive and make sure everyone feels heard. Sometimes I might overthink things a little, just wanting to make sure I handled a situation the best way possible, but I think that just means I care about doing a good job. 

It's completely normal to want to be polite and make a good impression, isn't it, Doctor? I've always tried to be the kind of person others feel comfortable talking to. I wouldn't want you to think I'm antisocial or anything like that. I've always been very capable socially.
Do you believe that certain events, messages, or coincidences have a special hidden meaning meant specifically for you?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I know sometimes people read into things a bit too much, like maybe thinking a song on the radio is playing just for them, but I don't do that. I've always been a very grounded person, very practical. You have to be practical when you're managing a retail floor, you know? 

I just focus on my work and my daily routine. If I see a coincidence, I just think, well, that's a funny coincidence, and I move on. I don't go looking for hidden messages or anything strange like that. I've always been very level-headed. 

It's better to just take things at face value, don't you agree, Doctor? I wouldn't want you to think I'm letting my imagination run away with me or anything. I'm very sensible about those kinds of things.
Have you become much less interested in other people or in spending time with them over the past six months?

Well, um... no, I don't think so. I still really value my relationships. I mean, when you're a supervisor in retail, you're constantly talking to people all day long, so... sometimes by the time I get home, I might just want a quiet evening to rest my feet and catch my breath. 

But that's just normal exhaustion from the job, you know? It's not that I don't want to be around anyone. I still care very much about my friends and my team at the store. I always make it a point to be friendly and stay in touch, because being a good friend is important to me. 

Everyone needs a little time to recharge after a busy week, don't they, Doctor? I certainly haven't stopped caring about people or lost interest in them, I promise you that. I'm still the same friendly guy I've always been.
Have you ever heard voices that other people could not hear?

Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely not. I know that's something that happens to some people, and it sounds very frightening, but I've never experienced anything like that. 

My hearing is perfectly fine, just the usual sounds of the store—the registers beeping, the music on the overhead, people chatting. Sometimes I might think I hear my name being called from another aisle, but it's always just a customer needing help or one of my associates looking for me. That's just the nature of a busy retail environment, you know? 

I wouldn't want you to worry that I'm... hearing things that aren't there. I'm very grounded in reality. That's a good thing, right, Doctor? To just be focused on the real world around me?
Do you ever feel like your thoughts are being broadcast aloud so that other people can hear them?

Oh, goodness, no. No, my thoughts are strictly my own. I mean, could you imagine? In my line of work, if people could actually hear what you were thinking when a customer is being a bit... difficult... well, I wouldn't have a job for very long! 

But seriously, no, I've never felt anything like that. I pride myself on keeping a very professional demeanor on the floor. I suppose sometimes people might be able to read my face if I'm feeling a bit stressed, but my actual thoughts are completely private. 

That's a sign of a healthy mind, isn't it, Doctor? Just knowing the boundary between what's in your head and what's out in the world? I always try to be very appropriate and keep my personal thoughts to myself. I certainly wouldn't want to make anyone uncomfortable. I'm doing okay on these questions, aren't I?
When you talk, do other people have trouble following you because your words come out jumbled or disconnected?

Well... I always try to be an excellent communicator. You really have to be, as a supervisor. But, um... I suppose... well, that is actually part of why I came in to see you. Just a minor thing, really, I don't want to make a big fuss out of it. 

It’s just that sometimes lately, when I try to explain the inventory numbers or go over the weekend schedule with the team, my words sort of... get ahead of me. I'll start talking about the delivery trucks, and then somehow I'm mentioning Thursdays, and then the church grill, or maybe my boss’s tone of voice... all kind of running together. 

I've noticed my associates looking at me like they can’t quite follow what I’m saying. It's a little embarrassing, if I'm being honest. But I really think it's just because I have so much on my plate at the store, you know? Anyone’s thoughts would jump around a bit when they’re juggling that many responsibilities. That’s perfectly understandable, isn't it, Doctor? I just need to remember to slow down and pace myself better, right?
In the past six months, have you noticed feeling or showing much less emotion than you used to?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I've always been a pretty even-keeled person, you know? It's important in retail not to let your emotions get the better of you, especially when dealing with the public. 

I mean, I still laugh at a good joke, and I certainly care about my team and my work. I wouldn't say I'm completely flat or anything like that. I just try to maintain a calm and professional demeanor. Maybe sometimes I'm a little tired after a long shift and don't have as much energy to, you know, be overly expressive, but that's just normal fatigue, right? 

I think being steady and reliable is a good quality for a supervisor. You want someone who can keep their cool, don't you think? I certainly wouldn't say I've lost my emotions... I'm just very good at managing them appropriately. That's a positive thing, right, Doctor?
